knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The textbook warning and the operating practice both say the pump must be off because the suction at the skimmer is powerful enough to cause injury.
Hoses, cables and cleaners are taken beyond the pool edge prior to swimming, because they can entangle a swimmer. Leaving any part in the water is not acceptable.
Vacuum to waste bypasses the filter and lowers the level, so overfilling first and topping up afterwards is the required practice.

practicalCriteria: The vacuum line is filled gradually and the air removed before connection
The valves are balanced and the straining noise is stopped before cleaning
The head is moved slowly in overlapping passes with the pump not stopped mid-hose change
Any automated cleaner, hose and cable is removed and the removal is recorded
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of one vacuuming visit with method and route
Assessor observation sign-off on hose set-up and removal of equipment
Photo of cleaner removal where the owner agrees
stopWorkCriteria: Hose connected to a running pump at the skimmer
Automated cleaner or cable left in the water while people swim
Household chemicals or wire brushes used on a liner
